children: The Singapore dollar consolidates against its U.S. counterpart ahead of MAS's policy statement and Singapore's advance 3Q GDP estimates due Wednesday. Singapore's "resilient growth and persistent inflation pressures, including risks from higher oil prices, continue to support the case for further calibrated tightening" by the MAS, two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a report. With expectations for another slight policy tightening by MAS already mostly priced in, however, "immediate SGD reaction may be muted," the strategists add. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 1.2803 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
